newsitem.title: INDIA: India pledges $93 mln to save Kashmir environment.
newsitem.headline: India pledges $93 mln to save Kashmir environment.

text.p: India will spend 3.34 billion rupees cleaning up Kashmir's famous lakes degraded by seven years of separatist violence, officials said on Tuesday.

"The glory of Kashmiri lakes and forests in Jammu and Kashmir is dwindling. The central government will initially spend 3.34 billion rupees ($93.3 million) to retrieve these water bodies," Environment Minister Saifuddin Soz told a news conference in Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir.
"I commit myself to help the Jammu and Kashmir government to do everything possible for conservation of forests and retrieving Dal and other lakes," Soz said.
"Our main focus will be Dal and next will be Wular Lake."
Wular, Asia's biggest fresh water lake, lies among pine forests some 55 km (33 miles) north of Srinagar.
The Environment Ministry plans to clean and remove weed from Dal Lake and also move houses built illegally, Soz said. India will use water-cleaning technology imported from Austria.
He said the government was already spending tens of millions of rupees to save the snow leopard and black neck crane in the state's remote Ladakh region, and Kashmiri deer known as Hangul.

Kashmiri environmentalists say local authorities have neglected the Himalayan region's environment while battling the insurgency. Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have died in the violence.
Ornithologists say shrinking wetlands in Kashmir have deprived thousands of migratory birds of a winter habitat in the Himalayan valley. ($1=35.8 rupees)
